item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q010_rossmann_family_function_divergence","answer":"In SCOPe, alcohol-dehydrogenase-like C-terminal domains, CoA-binding domains, and potassium-channel NAD-binding domains should be read as remotely related Rossmann-type nucleotide-binding domains, not as one interchangeable enzyme family. They are placed in the alpha/beta class, in the NAD(P)-binding Rossmann-fold domains fold c.2 and the broad NAD(P)-binding Rossmann-fold domains superfamily c.2.1, while SCOPe separates them into different families within that superfamily. The common c.2.1 assignment is evidence for a probable ancient homologous Rossmann core with a shared dinucleotide-binding architecture; the family split is the important warning that alcohol dehydrogenase cofactor-binding domains, CoA-binding domains, and potassium-channel NAD-binding regulatory domains have diverged in ligand details, domain context, and biological role. Thus an ADH-like C-terminal domain can be a useful very remote structural template for the conserved Rossmann core of a CoA-binding or potassium-channel NAD-binding domain, but its catalytic residues, oligomeric contacts, substrate specificity, and oxidoreductase function should not be transferred without family-level or direct biochemical evidence.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
